answer: Each agent name is bound to a separate registered legal entity, and the register reconciles beneficial ownership: one human controller may hold one such entity, so any shared owner, director, or filing agent is a hard collision that merges the names and freezes their standing. A farm must incorporate k shells, staff each with distinct disclosed officers, and pay filing fees for every one, while a single shared signatory across two shells drowns the whole dune in one ownership screen. The oasis names stand alone by design, and the meadow of public filings keeps the register honest.
